What is SQL? SQL means Structured Query Language. It is used to communicate with a relational database. Simple Meaning SQL is the language used to create, change, protect, and ask questions from database tables.
Data Definition Language — defining database structure

SQL is the standard language for communicating with relational databases. DDL defines structure (CREATE, ALTER, DROP); DML manages data (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE). DCL controls access (GRANT, REVOKE); SELECT retrieves and filters data. Good SQL starts from good table design — normalize before writing queries. Always use WHERE with UPDATE and DELETE, and test with SELECT first.

DML is for data content. It answers: "What data should be added, changed, or deleted?"

DCL controls who can access or use the database.
DCL is about permissions and security. It answers: "Who is allowed to do what?"
Gives permission to a user or role to perform a specific action on a database object.
Removes permission from a user or role, revoking their access to a specific action.
TO student_user; -- Remove DELETE from student
A student account may be GRANTED SELECT access to view data but REVOKED DELETE access to prevent accidental or unauthorized removal of records.

The SELECT command retrieves data from one or more tables. Meaning A query is a question asked to the database. SELECT is the most common and frequently used query command. Rule Avoid SELECT * in final reports when possible. Choose only the columns you need for better performance. Result CustomerID CustomerName Ana Cruz Ben Reyes
-- Select specific columns SELECT CustomerID, CustomerName FROM Customers; -- Select all columns
Use WHERE to filter rows and ORDER BY to arrange results.
Filters rows based on a condition. Example: CustomerID = 1.
Sorts the result. ASC = ascending (default); DESC = descending. Common Operators = <> > < > = < =
JOIN combines related rows from different tables.
Orders.OrderID, Customers.CustomerName, Orders.OrderDate FROM Orders JOIN Customers
JOIN uses key columns to connect tables. CustomerID connects Orders to Customers.
The ON condition should match the primary key of one table to the foreign key of another table.
INNER JOIN returns only matching rows. Other types: LEFT JOIN, RIGHT JOIN, FULL JOIN — each handles non-matching rows differently.

Good database practice includes careful commands and clear naming. Forgetting the semicolon in systems that require it. Using UPDATE or DELETE without a WHERE clause. Misspelling table or column names. Putting many values in one cell instead of normalizing.
Joining tables without the correct key relationship.

Good SQL starts from good table design. If the table is messy, the query becomes difficult.
A normalized design separates one topic per table. Customers CustomerID (PK) CustomerName Ana Cruz Ben Reyes Orders OrderID (PK) CustomerID (FK) OrderDate
Why Better? Each row has one clear record. Keys connect the tables (CustomerID links Customers → Orders; OrderID links Orders → OrderItems). This makes queries easier, faster, and more accurate.
DDL commands define or change database objects such as tables, columns, and constraints. Meaning
DDL is for database structure. It answers: "What tables and columns should exist?"
Make a new database object (table, index...)
Remove all rows from a table (keeps structure)
DDL usually changes the design. Use it carefully because it may affect the whole database. DROP and TRUNCATE cannot be easily undone.
